readme_content:
# STRUM — Small Team Reconnaissance Urban Missions

A two-person collaborative (dyadic) neuroergonomics dataset: pairs of participants
perform a team urban-reconnaissance "satmap" task while a time-synchronized multimodal
sensor suite records **both** members simultaneously via Lab Streaming Layer (LSL), one
`.xdf` recording per session. Collected at the recording laboratory.

Originating study: [citation withheld for anonymous review].

## Dyadic layout — read this first

STRUM records **two participants per session into one recording**, a layout BIDS has no
native construct for (a `sub-` is exactly one organism). This dataset models the dyad as
**metadata, not hierarchy**:

- **Each human is its own `sub-`.** The two members of a session do not share a subject
  directory.
- The pairing lives in **`participants.tsv`**:
  - `pair_id` — the dyad both members share (e.g. `01`);
  - `partner_id` — the `participant_id` of the other member;
  - `station` — the acquisition seat (`Delta` / `Echo`) the participant occupied.
- **Per-participant** signals (that participant's EEG / EMG / ECG / EOG / auxiliary channels,
  their eye/scene/video, their force plate) live under their own `sub-`.
- **Shared / world** streams (PhaseSpace motion capture of both bodies, the game's SNAP
  task events, audio) are **duplicated identically into both partners'** trees, written
  from a single extraction. Event sidecars and HED record which agent each event refers
  to (self / partner / AI).

See `participants.json` for the full column definitions.

**Split by pair, not by participant.** Both members of a session were recorded
simultaneously — same room, same task events, one shared clock — so the two `sub-` entries
of a pair are **not independent samples**. A plain participant-level split
(`train_test_split(participants, …)`) puts one member in train and their partner in test:
on this roster a seeded 20% split leaves about a third of the pairs straddling the two sets
(11 of 33 at the median, up to 13). Performance is then inflated and nothing in the data
warns you. Group on `pair_id` — equivalently `session`, since each session holds exactly one
pair and no participant appears in more than one — using a grouped splitter such as
scikit-learn's `GroupShuffleSplit` or `GroupKFold`. The same key must travel with any
windows, epochs or segments derived from a recording. With only 33 pairs a held-out fold is
6–7 pairs, so report spread rather than a single mean. Dyad-aware splitters and a leakage
check are in [`[withheld for review]/starter-pack`]([repository withheld for review]/starter-pack).

## De-identified identifiers

Published labels are **sequential and de-identified**, assigned deterministically:

- `participant_id` → `sub-001`, `sub-002`, … (ordered by the original study id).
- `pair_id`, and the BIDS session entity → `01`, `02`, … / `ses-01`, … (one per dyad).

They are **not** the original STRUM study/session ids. The source records are keyed by
both a subject id and a session id, so neither is published as a label; the
original↔published mapping is kept in a **private crosswalk that is not part of this
release**. This breaks the public→source linkage while preserving full internal
traceability.

## Station identity

The recordings bind each participant's data to a **station** (`Delta` / `Echo`) but carry
no hardware identity tag — the amplifier trigger lines are empty and synchronization is
LSL-only. The station↔participant binding therefore comes from the acquisition run-sheet
(corroborated by recording dates and peripheral notes), not from the recordings alone,
and is recorded in `participants.tsv` `station`.

## Scope

The participant roster covers the full known set: **33 sessions / 66 participants** (31
canonical sessions plus two early pilot sessions). `participants.tsv` lists every
participant with `station` (acquisition run-sheet) and `age` / `sex` / `handedness`
(de-identified demographics — date of birth and all other survey fields were dropped at
source). Modality data files are present for the full roster and BIDS-validated (see
*Conversion status*).

Most sessions are a single run; a few carry a second acquisition block (`run-2`). The
scalp montage varies by session (one early session uses a smaller layout; the rest use a
high-density BioSemi cap). Eye-tracking is present for both stations in most sessions but
only the `Delta` participant in a few. Per-subject specifics (channels, electrode
positions, runs) are recorded in the BIDS sidecars as each modality is added.

**Note on participant counts.** The originating paper reports 56 participants in 28 pairs
with 3 sessions excluded, and a sex breakdown ("13 f, 49 m" = 62) that does not reconcile
with the 56 total. This conversion includes every available session and never invents a
value; the discrepancy is flagged for reconciliation and is not resolved here.

## Modalities

Per participant unless noted:

- **EEG** — BioSemi high-density scalp EEG (montage varies by session), 512 Hz → `eeg/`.
  One recording is the exception: `sub-009` `ses-05` `run-1` was acquired at **2048 Hz**
  (1 of 80 recordings). `SamplingFrequency` in each `*_eeg.json` is authoritative — do
  not assume a single rate across the dataset.
- **EMG** — 43-channel neckband → native `emg/`.
- **ECG / EOG / auxiliary** — BioSemi external channels → `eeg/`; ECG and EOG are typed,
  the remaining auxiliary (`AUX`) channels are typed `MISC` (originally described as a
  respiration belt in the source study, not re-verified in this release).
- **Motion** — PhaseSpace motion capture of both bodies, 480 Hz, *shared* → `motion/`;
  plus each player's in-game avatar pose (resampled to 50 Hz).
- **AI agents (game environment)** — the game populates the scene with scripted AI
  characters. Their coordinates are kept in `sourcedata/` **only, not as a modality**,
  because they are part of the **ambient environment**: they follow fixed routes and do
  **not** interact with the participants. Retained for anyone studying the visual scene.
- **Eye-tracking** — head-mounted gaze / scene / AOI per station; *optional* per session,
  present for **43 of 66 participants**.
- **Physio** — AMTI force plate → `*_physio`.
- **Behavior / events** — Xbox controller (axes as physio, buttons as events), scores,
  and the SNAP task marker timeline → `beh/` + `events.tsv` (HED-annotated last). Mouse
  and keyboard were **dropped** (verified unused — the task is controller-driven).
- **Audio / video** — identifiable human-subjects media with no native BIDS datatype;
  **restricted**: kept in `sourcedata/av/` (outside the subject tree), so they are not part
  of the released subject data.

## Data conventions & notes

A few dataset-wide conventions and known data gaps, so downstream users are not surprised:

- **Task events live in `eeg/`.** Each run has a single `*_events.tsv` (in the participant's
  `eeg/` folder) derived from the SNAP task-marker stream on the shared LSL clock. Because the
  events are one task timeline — not EEG-specific data — they are **not** duplicated into the
  `motion/`, `emg/`, or `beh/` folders; the events for a run apply to **all** simultaneously
  recorded streams of that run. HED annotation is a per-task `task-<label>_events.json`
  sidecar, inherited by every run.
- **Scalp montage varies by session** — `channels.tsv` is authoritative per recording. Three
  total-channel layouts appear: the standard high-density BioSemi cap (238 channels incl.
  auxiliaries), an AIB-augmented variant (270 = 238 + 32, eight participants), and one early
  small-cap session (fewer scalp electrodes but 281 total channels).
- **Force plate: per participant, occasionally absent.** Each seat has an AMTI force plate,
  but eight participant-runs have **no force data** — that plate produced zero samples at
  acquisition (a hardware dropout, verified against the source recordings) while the partner's
  plate recorded normally. Those seats simply omit the `recording-force` physio file.
- **EEG/EMG BDF record blocking.** BDF stores data in whole-second records, so a recording's
  BDF may be padded by **under one second** at the end; `RecordingDuration` in the `*_eeg.json`
  / `*_emg.json` sidecar gives the true recorded duration.
- **Query wording is missing for half the queries.** For `query_created` events the raw
  marker carries a `phrase:` field with the question as it was put to the participant. In
  two categories the task software wrote the memory address of a Python function there
  instead of the text (`phrase:"<function <lambda> at 0x22AD1170>"`), so that wording is
  lost — it was never recorded. This is in the source recordings, not the conversion, and
  cannot be recovered. Affected: **`sound_direction` (5,111 events, all of them)** and
  **`audiocomm` (292 events, about 45% of that category)**; `color`, `direction` and `viewside` are unaffected —
  5,403 of 10,807 `query_created` events in total. Every other field of those events is
  intact, so the trials remain fully usable: `category` gives the question type,
  `answer` the correct response, and the raw marker's `all_answers` the alternatives
  offered. Only the literal question text is unavailable.
- **Spoken sentences are identified by index, not text.** `stimulus_language_spoken`
  events carry a numeric utterance index (1–618) rather than the words, because the task
  played pre-recorded audio and logged the file number; the audio and any transcript are
  not part of this dataset. The index is still informative: it is stable, so the same
  index is the same utterance; target and probe utterances are indices 1–200 while
  distractors span 1–618; for statements an index of **100 or below marks a true
  statement** and above 100 a false one; and for distractors the index range identifies
  which of the four speakers spoke, each fixed at its own spatial angle (1–154 speaker 1
  at -0.9 rad, 155–309 speaker 4 at +2.3, 310–465 speaker 2 at +0.9, 466–618 speaker 3
  at -2.3). By contrast `stimulus_language_written` events carry the **full sentence
  text** in the raw marker, and `stimulus_auditory` events name the sound
  semantically (`car engine`, `child`, `dog bark`, `pot`, `chicken cluck`).

## Conversion status

**All modalities are converted and individually validated across the full roster** (33
sessions / 66 participants), and the dataset passes the official BIDS validator with **no
errors**. HED annotation of the task events is complete. The conversion is deterministic and
re-runnable from the read-only source recordings.

Per-modality coverage — where a count is below 66, the missing seats are genuine
source-data absences (a station or stream not recorded that session), never dropped data:

| Modality | Coverage | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| EEG | 66/66 | scalp EEG + external ECG/EOG/aux channels |
| EMG | 64/66 | one early session used a small cap with no neckband |
| Motion (PhaseSpace) | 66/66 | shared room-scale capture, duplicated to both members |
| Motion (in-game avatar) | 66/66 | per-player pose, resampled to 50 Hz |
| Force plate | 57/66 | per-seat AMTI plate; absent where the plate recorded no samples (hardware dropout) |
| Controller | 63/66 | three seats had no controller-axes stream recorded |
| Eye-tracking | 43/66 | head-mounted gaze/scene/AOI; optional per session |
| Task events | 66/66 | SNAP marker timeline in `eeg/*_events.tsv` (HED-annotated) |
| Audio / video | restricted | identifiable; in `sourcedata/av/`, not released |

## Block partitioning

This tree is a **re-partition of the full-session recordings** (the
`STRUM-bids-fullsessions` dataset): every session recording is cut into its
constituent **blocks** and **lulls**, one file per segment per modality. Sessions
remain the directory level; only filenames change (`task-satmap_run-1` -> a block or
lull label). It is produced from the converted BIDS tree (never the raw source) by
`strum_bids.blocks`, deterministically.

### This tree does not reassemble into the sessions

The blocks and lulls together are **not** the whole recording. A session's material that
belongs to no block and to no lull -- setup and teardown before the first and after the
last block, and the inter-block gaps of sessions whose pauses carry no lull marker -- is
not in any file here. Concatenating every block and lull of a session therefore yields
slightly less than the original recording, and the pieces are cut per member on that
member's own EEG-anchored clock, so they do not line up sample-for-sample across the two
members either.

Nothing is lost from the dataset: the full-session tree remains the complete record, and
anything needing continuous data across a block boundary should be taken from there. Use
this tree when the unit of analysis is a block or a lull.

### Which files to use (read this first)

Most analyses want only the clean, fully-identified blocks. **Select them with one glob
on `acq-complete`** -- this automatically excludes every truncated / restart-split block
AND every ambiguous `task-blockunknown` block (those are always `acq-partial`):

```
# analysis-ready canonical blocks only:
<dataset>/sub-*/ses-*/**/*_acq-complete_*
# the inter-block pauses (no acq entity), if you want them:
<dataset>/sub-*/ses-*/**/*_task-lull_*
```

The complement, `*_acq-partial_*`, is exactly the set you may want to skip: blocks that
were cut short by the recording start/end or a restart, sit on a restart-renumbered
(untrusted) boundary, or whose mission content is ambiguous (`task-blockunknown`, no
canonical letter). They are **kept and clearly marked, never silently dropped**, so the
choice is yours -- but if in doubt, use `acq-complete` only.

**Blocks** carry a canonical letter (`task-block<A-E>`), assigned by mission content,
not the task software's emitted index (which a recording restart re-numbers):

  - **task-blockA** = canonical block 0 (missions: indiv-pan-watch, indiv-watch-drive, coop-movetogether, indiv-watch-pan, indiv-drive-watch, coop-aerial-vehicle)
  - **task-blockB** = canonical block 1 (missions: coop-movetogether, coop-vehicle-aerial, indiv-drive-watch, coop-secureperimeter)
  - **task-blockC** = canonical block 2 (missions: coop-secureperimeter, indiv-watch-pan, indiv-pan-watch, coop-vehicle-aerial, coop-aerial-vehicle, indiv-watch-drive)
  - **task-blockD** = canonical block 3 (missions: indiv-drive-watch, indiv-pan-watch, coop-vehicle-aerial, coop-aerial-vehicle, indiv-watch-pan)
  - **task-blockE** = canonical block 4 (missions: indiv-drive-watch, coop-vehicle-aerial, coop-aerial-vehicle, coop-movetogether)
  - **task-blockunknown** = a block whose mission content is an ambiguous prefix
    shared by >1 canonical block, so no letter can be assigned; always `acq-partial`.

**`acq-complete` vs `acq-partial`.** A block is `acq-complete` only when it is the full,
trusted canonical sequence. It is `acq-partial` when truncated by the recording start or
end, interrupted by a restart, sitting on an untrusted (restart-renumbered) boundary, or
ambiguous. Partial blocks are **retained, not dropped**, so they can be excluded with a
single glob (`*_acq-complete_*`) when unwanted.

**Lulls** (`task-lull_run-<N>`) are the inter-block pauses, numbered in time order
within each member's session. They are deliberately **not** called `rest`: participants
remain seated, instrumented, and may be talking.

**`run-` entity.** Present only for genuine repetition -- when the same canonical block
occurs more than once for a member in a session (e.g. split across a recording restart),
those instances become `run-1`, `run-2`. Otherwise no `run-` entity appears on blocks.

**Timing.** Each cut is re-zeroed to its own file start. EEG/EMG are cut on
whole-second BDF record boundaries (lossless byte copy; `n_records`/`RecordingDuration`
updated), so a block's first sample may precede its nominal onset by up to one record --
the events and physio `StartTime` are re-zeroed to the *actual* file start, preserving
that sub-record residual rather than absorbing it. Motion/physio/events tile exactly.
Each member is cut on its own EEG-anchored timeline (the same dyad marker has different
onsets in the two members' files).
